claims.text: Bare CoCrFeNi exhibits inconsistent and relatively high friction and wear during sliding over a wide temperature range.
An ultrathin multilayer adaptive coating on CoCrFeNi will remain stable from room temperature to 800 °C.
The coating will form a lubricious tribolayer in situ during sliding.
The tribolayer will be self-replenishing and sustained as temperature and load change.
Sliding will cause controlled oxidation and phase transformation within the coating.
Controlled oxidation and phase transformation will produce a continuous low-shear-strength film.
The tribofilm will reduce direct asperity contact and interfacial shear stress.
The tribofilm will suppress adhesive and oxidative wear.
Coated CoCrFeNi will maintain lower friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The coating will reduce the coefficient of friction by at least 20% relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi across the full temperature range.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have lower wear volume or wear rate than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The intervention will remain effective under multiple low and high normal loads in ambient oxidizing air.
Rapid thermal cycling and highly corrosive environments may lie outside the coating's effective regime.
Nanohierarchical architecture in Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 can provide ultralow wear from room temperature to 800 °C through temperature-dependent adaptive interface protection.
Y2O3-modified Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 composite coatings can reduce high-temperature friction, mass loss, oxidation, and wear damage.

contradictions.description: The predicted wear outcome is only described as significantly reduced, whereas the falsification rule requires at least an order-of-magnitude wear-rate improvement. Thus, the experiment could falsify the hypothesis despite observing the less specific improvement actually predicted.
